title: A continuous map from a profinite group to a discrete space is invariant under an open normal subgroup
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group and let $S$ be a discrete topological space. If $f:G\to S$ is continuous, then there is an open normal subgroup $U\subseteq G$ such that $f(xu)=f(x)$ for all $x\in G$ and $u\in U$.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous, the remark that continuity into a discrete space is equivalent to open stabilizers; the profinite compactness and open-normal-basis argument is supplied by the agent

proof.text: For each x in G, let W_x = {a in G | f(xa) = f(x)}. This is an open neighbourhood of 1: it is the preimage of the open singleton {f(x)} under the continuous map a ↦ f(xa). Mathlib ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one supplies an open normal subgroup H_x contained in W_x. The open cosets x H_x cover G, since 1 belongs to H_x. Compactness (isCompact_univ.elim_finite_subcover) gives a finite set t of these cosets covering G. The set t is nonempty, since the cover contains 1.

Let U be the finite infimum of the open normal subgroups H_y for y in t, formed with Finset.inf'. Then U is an open normal subgroup and U ≤ H_y for every y in t (Finset.inf'_le). Given x in G and a in U, choose y in t and b in H_y with x = yb. Both b and ba belong to H_y, hence f(yb) = f(y) = f(y(ba)). Associativity gives f(xa) = f(x). The neighbourhood subgroups are already normal, so no separate normal-core construction is needed.
